criteria.criterion: The change description names the root cause: the driver has only a fixed deadline and no progress tracking or stall detection. The fix is in the driver loop in crates/athena-agent/src/claude.rs, with the reason string built in procs.rs next to deadline_reason.
criteria.evidence: The CHANGELOG entry says: "Root cause: the driver enforced only a fixed deadline (1800s for the producer) and tracked no progress, so a stalled agent burned the whole deadline". A comment in the loop states the same cause (claude.rs:365-366). The check is in the invoke loop at claude.rs:383-385. stall_reason and stall_window are defined in procs.rs right after deadline_reason. The commit message is only "candidate", so the description lives in the CHANGELOG entry.

criteria.criterion: A new test in crates/athena-agent/src/claude.rs uses a fake agent that emits one line and then goes silent, with a long timeout. It asserts that the run ends well before the timeout with outcome TimedOut and a detail naming a stall (no progress). It fails on the base commit and passes with the change. Run: cargo test -p athena-agent.
criteria.evidence: a_silent_agent_is_stopped_early_as_stalled_not_at_the_deadline passed. It uses the stand-in in "hang" mode, which prints lines and then runs sleep 60, with a 15s timeout. It asserts that the run took less than 12s, that the outcome is TimedOut, and that the detail contains "no progress for 5s". I did not run it on the base commit, because that would change git state. From the code it cannot pass there: the min_stall_window field does not exist on the base commit (compile error), and the base loop only stops the run at the 15s deadline, which breaks the under-12s assertion.

criteria.criterion: A second test shows an agent that keeps emitting lines, slowly but within the stall window, is not stopped early and still completes. It proves slow is told apart from stalled, so the fix covers the class and not one job.
criteria.evidence: a_slow_agent_that_keeps_emitting_is_not_stopped_as_stalled passed. In "slow" mode the stand-in prints a line every 2s, four times (about 8s in total), against a 5s window. The test asserts Success and wall_s > 5.0, so new activity resets the window rather than a fixed 5s from the start ending the run.

criteria.criterion: The existing deadline test (detail 'deadline of 2s reached') still passes unchanged, and an agent that is silent for the whole timeout still reports the deadline reason when the stall window is not shorter than the timeout.
criteria.evidence: a_timed_out_invocation_is_timed_out_with_a_lower_bound passed, and the diff does not touch it. It runs a silent "hang" agent with a 2s timeout. The window there is the 60s floor (stall_window(2s, 60s) = 60s, as a_stall_window_is_never_shorter_... also asserts), so the deadline fires first and the detail stays "deadline of 2s reached".

criteria.criterion: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo test (whole workspace) all pass.
criteria.evidence: Athena's recorded checks on this tree: fmt passed, clippy passed with -D warnings, and the test suite passed with 1460 tests.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing the stall watchdog and its window.
criteria.evidence: There is a new entry under Added: "A stall watchdog in the agent driver ... when none appears for a third of the timeout (600s at 1800s), never less than 60s."

findings.summary: A single long tool call can be mistaken for a stall, because the window is not checked against the configured Bash timeouts.
findings.evidence: Activity is only a stdout line. athena.toml sets bash_default_timeout_ms = 600000 and bash_max_timeout_ms = 1200000. The stall window is timeout/3: 1000s for the producer (3000s), 800s for the verifier (2400s), 100s for the reader (300s) and 200s for the planner and critic (600s). If Claude Code prints nothing while a tool runs, a legitimate long command (for example a cold full cargo test) would be killed early as "stalled". That is the slow-versus-stalled confusion the request asked to remove. The accepted reading chose "any stdout line" as activity, so this is a later improvement, not a blocker. One option is a window of at least the Bash max timeout plus a margin. This is a judgement from reading the code and config; I did not test it against a real Claude Code stream.

findings.summary: When the stall window has passed and the kill switch is on at the same moment, the run is reported as TimedOut, not Killed.
findings.evidence: The stall check runs before registry.stopped() in the if/else chain, the same order as the existing deadline check.

summary: I recommend pass. The change fixes the cause where it starts: the driver loop that every role uses (ClaudeCodeDriver::invoke in crates/athena-agent/src/claude.rs). That loop used to enforce only the fixed deadline. Now it records when the agent last wrote a line on its stream. If nothing arrives for a third of the timeout (never less than 60s), it ends the run as TimedOut with the detail "no progress for Ns (stalled)". stall_window and stall_reason sit in procs.rs next to deadline_reason. There is no new invocation field, no new outcome variant and no schema change. I ran `cargo test -p athena-agent --locked stall` and `cargo test -p athena-agent --locked claude::stand_in_tests`; all 9 stand-in tests pass. They include a silent agent stopped early as stalled, a slow but steady agent that is not stopped, the window formula, and the unchanged "deadline of 2s reached" test. fmt, clippy and the full test suite passed in Athena's recorded checks. I could not run the base commit, because that would change git state. From reading the code, the new stall test cannot pass there: the min_stall_window field does not exist on the base commit, and the old loop would only stop the silent agent at the 15s deadline. All 3 changed files are on the deliverables list. One minor risk remains. Claude Code may send nothing on the stream while a long tool call runs (this is an assumption about its stream behaviour, not something I tested). If so, a single long Bash call can be mistaken for a stall. The repository allows Bash calls of up to 1200s, but the windows are shorter: 1000s for the producer, 800s for the verifier, and 100s or 200s for the reader, planner and critic.
